sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ádammair appears as an Irish god. Some tales name him the sometime husband of Flidais, the goddess of the wild. In one region the paired name Ádammair Flidais marks a local figure in County Mayo. This figure links to the appetite of the hero Fergus mac Róich. Only Flidais could meet his inner hunger. Without her he needed seven women. Ádammair stays obscure next to his consort. Few myths belong to him alone.
objective: This article establishes Ádammair as the obscure Irish god husband of the woodland goddess Flidais.
